data.text: Aditi ChordiaAI meeting assistants take care of the boring stuff like note-taking, task creation, and follow-ups so you can focus on the actual conversation. I’ve been using a few of these tools myself and pulled together a list of the 5 best ones. Each offers solid AI features, useful integrations, and a free or freemium plan to get started. Let’s dive in.Top 5 AI Meeting Assistants to consider in 2026Avoma — for most advanced AI note-taking featuresOtter — for generating instant answers to questionsFireflies.ai — for team collaborationtl;dv — for AI-powered searchFathom — for basic transcription & summarization1. Avoma ‍If you want an AI meeting assistant that helps with your whole meeting workflow, Avoma is worth checking out. It can help you prepare agendas and schedule meetings. It also records and transcribes meetings automatically. Plus, it generates AI-powered notes and creates follow-up tasks for you.Key features of Avoma:Organized, in-depth AI-generated notes: Avoma identifies the topic of discussion and breaks it down into smart categories, such as business needs, pain points, competitors, etc. with timestamps linked to the conversation, so you can jump to the specific parts of the conversation rather than listening to the entire recording.Highly accurate transcription: Count for upwards of 95% accuracy with Avoma. No words are misspelled or sentences left halfway despite industry-specific jargon, heavy accents, and background noise.Collaborative note editor: Multiple people can collaborate in real-time, drop comments, tag members, and mark action items. You also have the option to take private notes—visible only to you.Searchable knowledge base: A centralized dashboard allows you to organize meetings under different folders and quickly search for calls or transcripts.Auto-chapters & question identification: Get deeper context into each section of the meeting with auto-chapters that break down the conversation into bite-sized video clips. You can also hover over to the questions tab to look at specific questions asked by the participants.Snippets: Need to capture a specific portion of the meeting and share it on Slack with the team members? With Snippets, you can highlight text from a conversation and create a video snippet instantly to share on any channel you like.Speaker insights & keyword tracking: Avoma identifies and differentiates speakers and tracks their talk time, talk-to-listen ratio, longest monologues, filler words, etc. You can also set alerts for keywords and track them on a daily/weekly/monthly basis.Wide variety of integrations: You can integrate Avoma with several video conferencing apps, dialers, collaboration tools, and CRMs. (Check out the complete list).‍‍Pros of Avoma:A forever free planEnd-to-end meeting lifecycle assistant—agenda setting, meeting scheduling, automatic recording & transcription, and follow-up action items.Highly accurate transcriptAdvanced AI note-taking with ‘smart categories’Centralized dashboard to organize and manage meetingsAvailable as a mobile appCons of Avoma:Not a basic AI transcriberDesigned for organizations. Not ideal for individuals, students, teachers, researchers, etcPricing:Avoma offers different plans designed to fit teams of all sizes, from startups to large organizations.You can also add extra features like conversation intelligence, revenue intelligence, and lead routing to get more insights and automate tasks.14 days free trial availableStartup: $19/user/monthOrganization: $29/user/monthEnterprise:  intelligence: $29/user/monthRevenue intelligence: $29/user/monthLead router: $19/user/monthWhat users say about Avoma:‍2. OtterOtter is an AI meeting assistant for teams that can record both in-person and virtual meetings, transcribe calls into text, and summarize meeting notes. What’s unique about Otter is that it can transcribe imported audio and video files from YouTube, Dropbox, etc., and export them into various file formats.Another thing Otter does differently is the Otter AI chat, which allows you to get up to speed on meetings by generating answers from discussions, meeting notes, and task lists in the workspace. Pros of Otter:Generate live summaries, highlight takeaways, and tag teammatesCreate follow-up emails and blog posts from AI-generated summariesCreate dedicated channels and add team membersSpeaker identification and basic keyword trackingCons of Otter:Low transcription accuracyHas no video support. It turns all the video recordings into audio filesExpensive compared to other AI meeting assistantsPricing:Free plan availablePro: $16.99/month per userBusiness: $30/month per userEnterprise: Contact for pricingWhat users say about Otter:‍3. Fireflies.ai‍Fireflies.ai has been around in the meeting AI assistant for a while. It allows you to transcribe meetings, send recaps, upload audio, and share or download transcripts. With Fireflies, you can organize team meetings with dedicated channels and store them for future reference. You can also sort the meetings by date, project, team, or topic to easily search for conversations on the dashboard.Pros of Fireflies.ai:AI-powered search for conversation snippets, keyword tracking, and moreTracks speaker talk time, key topics, sentiments, and monologuesCreates magic soundbites to share a specific part of the conversationAt any time, click on the chatbot AskFred to ask questions, key agenda, action items, and meeting overviewNative integration with video conferencing apps, CRMs, and collaboration platforms.Cons of Fireflies.ai:Doesn’t do a great job at summarizing meeting notesTranscriptions are more often not accurateStorage runs out quickly & the CS team is super aggressive in upselling premium plansPricing:Free plan availablePro: $18/month per userBusiness: $29/month per userEnterprise: $39/month per userWhat users say about Fireflies:‍3. tl;dvtl;dv is an AI notetaker that records and transcribes meetings from Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams. What I like about tl;dv is that you access a live transcript in the same window where the meeting is taking place. After the meeting is over, tl;dv generates a summary and relevant takeaways for each team member and ships it to them automatically.Pros of tl;dv:Intelligent AI-powered search to surface meetings & transcriptsUnderstands the topic of discussion and assigns meeting tagsHighlight notes, tag members, and assign action items within the transcriptGenerate weekly/monthly meeting summaries that list action items, next steps, etcCons of tl;dv:Limited storage and features on the free planOccasionally meeting summaries highlight irrelevant detailsDifficult to edit clips or soundbitesLacks browser supportPricing:Free plan availablePro: $29/month per userBusiness: $98/month per userEnterprise: Custom pricing availableWhat users say about tl;dv:‍5. FathomIf you’re looking for a free AI notetaker with basic features, Fathom is a great option. It can record, transcribe, highlight, and summarize meetings, as well as sync meeting notes to popular CRMs such as Salesforce and Hubspot. It also has native integrations with multiple collaboration and productivity platforms.Pros of Fathom:Automatically sync meeting summaries to CRMCreate clips from specific parts of the meeting and share them on SlackSet up daily/weekly alerts for specific keywords (available on the paid version)Create playlists of the best moments to coach your team (available on the paid version)Cons of Fathom:Basic AI transcriber with limited features (compared to the likes of Avoma, tl;dv, and Fireflies)Offers very few native integrationsExternal users need to create a Fathom account to access calls & transcriptTeam collaboration features are available only for premium plan usersDoesn’t record phone callsPricing:Free plan availablePremium: $15/month per userTeam Edition: $19/month per userTeam Edition Pro: $29/month per userWhat users say about Fathom:‍What to look for in an AI Meeting Assistant?Whether you need to generate transcripts, summarize notes, or extract key insights, these are the must-haves to look for in every AI meeting assistant:Integrations: You likely use other tools such as Google Calendar for scheduling meetings, ClickUp or Asana to manage tasks and collaborate with team members, and CRM to store customer data. Look for an AI meeting assistant that integrates with a wide variety of platforms to streamline your existing workflows and bring consistency to operations.Variety of AI features: Almost all AI meeting assistants can record and transcribe meetings. Look at the extra features they can offer you—AI-generated notes, sentiment analysis, topic breakdown, keyword tracking, and more. Of course, this will also depend on your use case and the capabilities you need.Pricing: Not all AI meeting assistants are created equally. Some are loaded with advanced features that you don't need, while others could be limiting. We suggest tools with either a freemium or a free plan so you can try them out before making a purchase.End-to-end automation: Very few AI meeting assistants offer features that automate the entire meeting experience—scheduling meetings, agenda setting, automatic recording and transcription, AI-generated notes, and CRM sync. In the long run, this helps you save time and improve team productivity.Collaboration features: Many platforms hide this behind a paywall, but you should be able to tag members, comment, and mark action items for seamless collaboration. At the same time, you should be able to store and organize meetings under different folders and search for calls/transcripts quickly.Make meetings more efficient with AI Meeting AssistantWith so many tools in the market, it can’t be easy to choose the one that aligns with your business needs, size, and budget. We hope that we did justice in relaying what each tool does best, so you can go ahead and try it for yourself, and decide which one is the best for you.Otter and Fireflies.ai are both great AI notetakers if you’re looking for simple transcription and note-taking. But at the same time, tl;dv and Avoma offer a better bang for your buck with advanced features available on the free plan. But if you’re looking for an all-in-one AI meeting assistant to automate your complete meeting workflow from scheduling meetings to automatic recording and transcription, AI-generated notes and summaries, and follow-ups, we recommend signing up for Avoma.And while you’re at it, also look at what our 1200+ users have to say about us.The all-in-won AI platform to automate note-taking, coaching, and moreThe all-in-won AI platform to automate note-taking, coaching, and moreGet started today.It just takes a minute to set up your account.No credit card is required.
